articles.title: Virgil van Dijk's role at Liverpool: Andoni Iraola's team are pressing high but is that a problem for their 35-year-old captain?
articles.summary: With Jamie Carragher suggesting on Monday Night Football that Liverpool are not playing to the strengths of their captain Virgil van Dijk, Adam Bate looks at the problems being created for the 35-year-old defender playing Andoni Iraola football behind this midfield...
articles.body:
During the first half there was a disagreement between Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk. The midfielder pressed but Como just passed the ball into the space behind him. Szoboszlai was visibly angry to find Van Dijk had not stepped up to close the gap.

Already, one game into the Premier League season, and even within five minutes of that particular game against Newcastle, there are signs that it could be a problem for Andoni Iraola. He wants his team to press high. But does his veteran captain want to do it too?

Van Dijk's failure to push up was a contributory factor in Newcastle's opener. Much was made of Anthony Elanga's 61-metre run for the goal but William Osula was able to feed him without anyone closing down, as Jamie Carragher pointed out on Sky Sports .

"Virgil van Dijk should be higher initially and if he is higher he could then make the challenge there," said Carragher. "But we are talking about a defender who is 35, coming towards the end of his career, one of the greatest players we have seen in that position."

It is a common trait with such players, as Carragher well knows. "It is very reminiscent of John Terry in that position. Do you remember John Terry under [Andre] Villas-Boas? He does not want to go in there. So you have almost got to play to the strengths of him."

He added of Van Dijk: "It is not just that Liverpool need protection in midfield and need more players there, he needs protection. This is probably the first season where he cannot help anyone else, he needs help himself." But will he get it in Iraola's system?

The Basque coach did a remarkable job in his three seasons with Bournemouth, building one of the most exciting sides in the Premier League. Iraola became renowned for his aggressive approach but it is a style that does place particular demands on his defenders.

A product of defending high is that there is often space behind. Bournemouth had the highest direct speed against of any team in the Premier League last season. That means opponents progressed the ball up the pitch quicker against them than anyone else.

At Liverpool, that could be an issue. Milos Kerkez was unable to catch Elanga but it hardly plays to the strengths of Van Dijk either. The Liverpool skipper had every quality required of a central defender in his prime but some attributes last longer than others.

He remains a formidable defender in both penalty boxes and boasts an impressive passing range with the ball at his feet anywhere on the pitch. But when out of possession on the halfway line, that can be an awkward spot even for elite ageing centre-backs.

There is some evidence to suggest that Van Dijk's speed is not quite what it once was. The fastest top speed that he has ever clocked in his Premier League career came during his debut season in the competition as a Southampton player following his move from Celtic.

His top speed in a Liverpool shirt was registered during the club's one title-winning campaign under Jurgen Klopp. But that is a long time ago now. Over the past three seasons prior to this one, Van Dijk's top speed has declined. It is not an asset for him now.

Van Dijk relies more than ever on his physicality and his intelligent positional play, but that becomes harder if the spaces that he is being asked to manage become bigger. And the problems only increase for Liverpool if those ahead press and he does not follow.

Any tension between Van Dijk and Szoboszlai that day lasted only for a moment and the Dutchman was fulsome in his praise of his team-mate after his penalty salvaged a point at Newcastle. He even talked up Szoboszlai's leadership skills. "He is here to take over."

But when will that be? After a season in which Mohamed Salah's status at Liverpool changed quicker than anyone could have anticipated, Van Dijk's role under Iraola is worth keeping an eye on. Because this Liverpool midfield is becoming an issue for him too.

Y es que Iván Martín coincidió con José Alberto y Chema Aragón en el Mirandés en la temporada 2020-21 y fue clave para elegir al Racing. Con él crecemos mucho”. Iván Martín Núñez nació en Bilbao (Vizcaya) el 14 de febrero de 1999 y dio el salto al fútbol profesional en la disciplina del Villarreal CF después de completar su formación en la cantera grogueta.  En verano de 2020 fue cedido al Club Deportivo Mirandés, donde coincidió con José Alberto, un año después militó, también a préstamo, en el Deportivo Alavés -con el que se estrenó en Primera ante el Real Madrid en Mendizorroza- para, en 2022, firmar con el Girona FC, donde ha jugado las últimas cuatro temporadas.

articles.summary: El jugador del Levante tiene el interés del extranjero que estarían dispuestos a cerrar una operación necesaria para las cuentas granotas
articles.body: La ausencia de Carlos Álvarez en El Sadar no ha pasado desapercibida para nadie. El jugador andaluz es una de las grandes perlas del Levante y un nombre propio marcado en rojo para que los del barrio de Orriols puedan hacer caja en este mercado de verano. Ni las autorizadas explicaciones que argumentó Luís Castro tras el partido ante Osasuna han caído en saco roto. El entrador granota explicó que la ausencia del atacante en el choque era “por una decisión personal, ya que necesitábamos otra cosa”. Seguidamente, matizó que “todos los jugadores del Levante, y yo también, estamos preparados para salir”. Ante este escenario, según ha adelantado RADIO MARCA Valencia y ha podido confirmar MARCA, la entidad granota espera una oferta por el jugador en los próximos días de un equipo extranjero. Así mismo, tanto Carlos Álvarez como el club, que son conscientes de esta situación, confirmarían su marcha si llega una oferta consensuada. El mediapunta de Sanlucar la Mayor, aterrizó en el Ciutat de Valencia en el verano de 2023, con el equipo en Segunda División, a coste cero procedente del Sevilla FC. Tras dos temporadas en la categoría de plata, donde mostró un rendimiento extraordinario, y un notable rendimiento en primera el curso pasado, el andaluz termina contrato en 2027 y a día de hoy no existe ningún tipo de negociación de renovación. Otro de los detalles, a destacar, de esta posible operación. Es que el cuadro hispalense se quedaría el 40% de una posible venta, aunque a partir de esta presente temporada, esa cantidad se rebajaría hasta el 30%.

articles.body: Chema Aragón, director deportivo del Racing reconocía en rueda de prensa de presentación de Iván Martín que Matteo Prati estaba prácticamente cerrado como nuevo futbolista del conjunto cántabro. Aragón dejaba claro que la negociación por el futbolista italiano se remonta al final de la pasada campaña, ' “Empezamos a hablar el 2 de junio y tuvimos que esperar tiempo para lo que nos hubiera gustado' . El futbolista de 22 años, que en la primera jornada de la Seie A no ha jugado con el Cagliari, está en negociaciones con el Racing ya desde la semana pasada, pero hasta ahora su fichaje no se había concretado. La duda es el si el eje del Cagliari llegaría al Racing en calidad de cedido o en propiedad. El conjunto cántabro quiere guardarse una opción de compra en caso que llegase a préstamo. La pasada temporada, en el mercado invernal, estuvo cedido (con opción de compra) en el Torino, también de la Serie A, aunque con un rol más discreto. Tiene contrato con su club hasta 2028. "El chico está entrenando mejor que nunca; y claro que influye lo que haga en estos partidos y es normal que tenga dudas", explicó, al tiempo que admitió que "cuando me preguntan digo que está el Real Madrid pero también está el Racing, que si le garantizara lo que tiene ahora, ser titular, seguro que se quedaría aquí". articles.title: Aston Villa: The reality of the finances available to Unai Emery at Villa Park following a summer of upheaval
articles.summary: Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett assesses the situation at Aston Villa following a summer of upheaval and a dismal 4-0 defeat to Brighton to start the 2026/27 season; Villa feel confident Emery's future is secure but top clubs have an admiration for the Spaniard
articles.body:
Last season was their most successful since 1982, when they won the old European Cup.

This time round, it was a Europa League win and a fourth-place Premier League finish - each of those achievements would have been enough to guarantee the riches and prestige of Champions League football.

Unai Emery was lauded as a hero by Villa fans even before last spring's spectacular, and rightly so.

He has won the Europa League title five times with three different clubs. A key question now is whether his downbeat assessment following the humbling by Brighton is indicative of a wider concern.

Clearly, Emery was upset with Ollie Watkins, and it currently seems a tall order for the striker to be reintegrated into the Villa squad, having made his desire to leave clear.

But more worrying is the overriding sense that Emery is struggling with the lack of options he has at his disposal right now.

After all that he has achieved at the club, his reward has been widespread disruption within the squad after four key player departures, potentially more to come, and limited finances.

Emery described it as having "had an intelligent market", amid efforts by the club to strengthen the squad before the deadline. "We know where we are and we know what we want to do again for the next year," he said.

There is mitigation for Villa's bosses, however, who have been frustrated by PSR rules, which they feel have been an ambition killer and stalled their progress.

The switch to Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) rules this season has only added to that and caused deeper resentment.

As regulars in European competition now, they are limited to spending 70 per cent of their football revenue on transfer fees and player wages.

Remember, they have already been fined twice by UEFA recently, being hit with a £9.5m penalty last year and a £19.4m fine in June, although £13m of that was suspended after Villa came to a settlement agreement.

That means, inevitably, Villa are a club that has to generate income from player trading in order to buy new talent.

The proof of that is in the figures from sales over the last three years; Villa have made over £410m selling the likes of Douglas Luiz, Jhon Duran, Jacob Ramsey and Moussa Diaby, before this summer's sale of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne.

Should Emiliano Martinez and Ollie Watkins follow, that number will be close to the half-a-billion mark, in terms of funds generated.

It is a big ask for Emery to see the castle that he has built taken down keystone by keystone, knowing he has to rebuild again. Last summer, the transfer upheaval contributed to the director of football Monchi leaving the club.

Importantly, Villa currently feel confident their manager is secure. After all, his contract has another three seasons to run, following the bumper new five-year deal he signed in May 2024.

But many of the biggest clubs in Europe have noticed with admiration the job Emery has done at Villa Park, and he will always be on the shortlist of the top clubs for as long as he keeps doing such a stellar job under the circumstances.

articles.title: 3 things to know about the Big 12, including why Texas Tech should roll even without Brendan Sorsby
articles.summary: The offseason story that dominated the Big 12 will turn out to not matter a single bit during the season.
articles.body:
The offseason story that dominated the Big 12 will turn out to not matter a single bit during the season.

Defending champion Texas Tech added Cincinnati QB Brendan Sorsby in one of the biggest transfer portal moves of January. But after Sorsby transferred, it became public that he had been betting on sports while in college. Those bets included Indiana games when he was a member of the Hoosiers.

As Sorsby (and, unofficially, Texas Tech) successfully pushed to remain eligible for the 2026 season, the rest of the Big 12 was up in arms.

All that consternation worked . Amidst the blowback, Sorsby said he'd explore his supplemental NFL Draft options and not play for the Red Raiders in 2026. The NFL, meanwhile, said that it wouldn't have a supplemental draft this summer and Sorsby will now effectively sit out both the 2026 college football and NFL seasons.

Got all that? Here's what you need to know about the Big 12.

Texas Tech vs. a team from Utah for the Big 12 title?

There are three clear favorites for two spots in the Big 12 championship game. And Texas Tech doesn't have to face either of its two main challengers in the regular season.

The Red Raiders are favorited for a second straight Big 12 title in part because of a schedule that might be the easiest in the conference. Tech's two toughest games on paper are both at home. Houston visits on Sept. 18, and Arizona comes to Lubbock on Halloween. The four opponents Texas Tech visits combined to win 16 games in 2025.

Sure, there's a real scenario where Texas Tech doesn't make the conference championship game. Maybe the quarterback position is unsettled after Sorsby's spring departure and Will Hammond isn't fully recovered from the torn ACL he suffered last season. Turnover regression could also hit hard. After being plus-1 in turnover margin in 2024, Texas Tech was plus-14 in 2025 as LB Jacob Rodriguez parlayed his penchant for turnovers into a fifth-place finish in the Heisman voting.

But we feel safe penciling in the Red Raiders.

From there, you can make a lot of cases for Texas Tech's opponent. The strongest two belong to BYU and Utah. The Utes host BYU on Nov. 7. But Utah is also entering a season without Kyle Whittingham in charge for the first time since Urban Meyer was the head coach in 2004.

Longtime Utah defensive coordinator Morgan Scalley takes over after years as Utah's coach in waiting. This is Scalley's first head coaching job and he's also got a new offensive coordinator after Jason Beck followed Whittingham to Michigan .

Scalley was able to keep quarterbacks Devon Dampier and Byrd Ficklin in Salt Lake City along with RB Wayshawn Parker . Utah should have one of the best rushing attacks in the country once again after averaging 266 yards and six yards per carry in 2025.

BYU is hoping for a second-year leap from QB Bear Bachmeier after he started as a true freshman in 2025. The QB who wears No. 47 totaled 26 touchdowns, but also had eight games with fewer than 200 passing yards. He's going to need to be a better passer in 2026. And he's also going to be doing it with some unfamiliar receivers. The return of RB L.J. Martin is huge, but no BYU receiver with more than 14 catches in 2025 is back on the roster.

The Cougars made a six-win jump from 2024 to 2025 and Arizona improved by five wins. We're bullish on both teams sustaining that level of success.

Houston brings back QB Conner Weigman for a second season after he threw for over 2,700 yards and rushed for 700 more. Weigman will provide a stable bridge to five-star freshman Keisean Henderson as Henderson is prepped to be the team's starter in 2027. Henderson, a native of Houston, was the top recruit in the state of Texas in 2026 and the No. 2 player overall behind Miami tackle Jackson Cantwell.

After losing top RB Dean Connors , Houston added former Tulane and Oregon rusher Makhi Hughes in the transfer portal. Hughes played for Willie Fritz at Tulane in 2023 when he rushed for 1,378 yards as a true freshman. After a 1,400-yard season in 2024, Hughes got just 17 carries in his lone season with the Ducks. The offensive line is full of experienced transfers and could be one of the best in the Big 12.

Arizona can claim it has the best QB in the conference in Noah Fifita . The fifth-year QB threw for over 3,200 yards and 29 TDs in 2025 as the Wildcats won their final five regular-season games. Head coach Brent Brennan added a host of power conference defenders in the transfer portal in an attempt to reload a unit that allowed just 19 points per game in 2025 after giving up over 30 in 2024.

The Wildcats could also be on the wrong side of some turnover regression, however. Arizona was plus-18 in turnovers after finishing plus-10 over their final four games of the season. Road trips to BYU and Texas Tech are also crucial to any playoff push.

Outside of those cats, Arizona State and TCU are the two teams with the best odds of sneaking into the title game. The Horned Frogs added former Harvard QB Jaden Craig to replace Josh Hoover , while former Kentucky QB Cutter Boley takes over in Tempe. TCU could have every opportunity to play its way into the Big 12 title game over the final two weeks of the season with games against Utah and Texas Tech.

Will Colorado or Oklahoma State have a bigger bounce-back?

Fourteen of the Big 12's 16 teams won at least five games in 2025. The two that didn't, Colorado and Oklahoma State, went 1-17 in conference play. The lone win was Colorado's 24-17 victory against Iowa State.

It's easier to make the case for an Oklahoma State rebound than it is for one for the Buffaloes. After firing Mike Gundy three weeks into the 2025 season, OSU hired Eric Morris from North Texas. The Mean Green offense was one of the most prolific in college football, and QB Drew Mestemaker , RB Caleb Hawkins and WR Wyatt Young are among the transfers who followed him to Stillwater. Mestemaker has emerged as an intriguing NFL Draft prospect after throwing for nearly 4,400 yards last year. Hawkins rushed for 1,434 yards and 25 TDs and Young had 70 catches for 1,264 yards and 10 TDs.

There may be some growing pains, but a schedule that doesn't include Arizona, Utah or BYU could be tailor-made for the Cowboys to make a bowl game.

The Buffaloes will have a good idea of where they stand among all power conference teams before Big 12 play begins thanks to road trips to Georgia Tech and Northwestern over the first three weeks of the season. QB Julian Lewis is the undisputed starter after getting playing time in 2025 as the Kaidon Salter experiment wasn't too successful.

Colorado has never figured out how to have a reliable rushing attack in Deion Sanders' tenure, and losing OT Jordan Seaton won't help those efforts. Former Alabama RB Richard Young is the latest player added to the backfield in an attempt to boost the run game and former Sacramento State head coach Brennan Marion is now the Buffaloes' offensive coordinator.

The defense is basically overhauled from a season ago. Colorado gave up just 23 points per game as it won nine games in 2024. It's allowed over 30 per game in Sanders' other two seasons in charge.

Defensive back Makari Vickers could end up as the Buffaloes' only starter on defense who wasn't added in the transfer portal, and the focus was on the front seven. Colorado gave up 223 rushing yards a game in 2025 and allowed over five yards a carry.

It's not impossible that the Buffaloes will be underdogs against every FBS team they face in 2026. Some upsets will be imperative.

articles.title: 2026 Fantasy Football: Smash that easy button with these 5 destination offenses that have narrow usage trees
articles.summary: The teams that employ the shortest list of contributors are the most appealing for fantasy football.
articles.body:
One of the keys to a happy adult life is learning how to deal with traffic. Maybe you're navigating a trip to the airport, or trying to find the most seamless work commute. I prefer to shop on off-peak hours, and take a late lunch in a mostly-empty restaurant. Less gridlock, more happiness.

Keep that theme in mind as you're doing your fantasy football scouting for 2026. The NFL teams that employ the shortest list of regular contributors become destination offenses for fantasy managers. Keep it narrow , keep it simple.

We want you to smash that easy button as often as possible. Let's explore a few offenses that should be fun this year, as they look to be productive regularly but tied to a limited number of contributors. These are your narrow-usage offenses for 2026.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

So long as starting QB Joe Burrow stays healthy, this Cincinnati offense could go to the moon. And there won't be many seats taken on that spaceship, as almost the entire offense will be funneled through two star receivers (Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins ) and one do-it-all running back ( Chase Brown ). The Bengals have also had a horrible defense for three years running; even if it's mildly improved, pinball games are probably coming to Cincinnati. That makes the Bengals a potential carnival team as well, checking all the fun boxes.

They're not a perfect fit for this frame, as Kyren Williams and Blake Corum share backfield work (I prefer to draft Corum at cost) and the tight end room is super-crowded. But the Rams throw to their backs less than any other team, and veteran QB Matthew Stafford does very little with his legs. Puka Nacua had a robust 30.29% market share last year, and Davante Adams led the NFL in both red-zone targets and touchdown catches. The Rams don't have an impactful third WR looming on the depth chart, which means Nacua and Adams will once again be swimming in targets.

Detroit checks so many boxes when we're searching for a bankable offense. There's plenty of continuity here, a schedule heavy on indoor games and a bunch of beatable defenses coming to town. Jared Goff is a reliable veteran QB but not a runner, which is good for his teammates.

Fantasy Football: 3 big-name quarterbacks we're fading at ADP this season

Fantasy Football: Justin Boone's backup running back rankings for 2026

Fantasy Football Running Back Scouting Reports: A preview of some of the RB profiles in the Yahoo Fantasy Ultra Playbook

Jahmyr Gibbs will have the backfield essentially to himself this year, slotting him as the consensus No. 1 pick. Amon-Ra St. Brown is a consistency king who fits in the middle of any first round. Jameson Williams took off last year when Sam LaPorta got hurt; this summer, we once again worry about a LaPorta injury. Even if the Big 4 all remain healthy, there's plenty to go around. Keep in mind second-year WR Isaac TeSlaa has been disappointing in camp, which tightens the overall concentration.

This one is a little tricky, as the Falcons haven't solved their QB problem yet. Tua Tagovailoa has been shaky this summer, and Michael Penix Jr. hasn't shown much through two seasons. But Atlanta didn't have great QB play last year, either, and Bijan Robinson , Drake London and Kyle Pitts Sr. were all fantasy stars. Robinson and Pitts saved the best for last; Robinson was the best RB in the fantasy playoffs, and Pitts went nuclear in Week 15 (11-166-3), one of the best tight end games of all-time.

After Atlanta's Big 3 are selected, most rooms will ignore the rest of the Falcons. RB Brian Robinson Jr. is merely an insurance play (and sometimes a name-confusion click) and no support receiver here is commanding a top-200 pick. The Falcons will lean on their best players again this fall, and we like it that way.

The Dallas vibes are similar to the Cincinnati vibes, a star quarterback and productive offense trying to outscore the mediocre defense on the other side. The concentration isn't quite as tight in Dallas, as four primary players see regular work ( CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , Javonte Williams , Jake Ferguson ), and Ryan Flournoy is an interesting third receiver. But Flournoy probably won't see a big role unless Lamb or Pickens get hurt, and QB Dak Prescott has cut back his running in the second half of his career. At the end of the day, we know where our Texas Toast is buttered.

articles.title: Pumas ficha a Chino Huerta para ‘olvidar’ a Efraín Juárez; así le ganaron a Toluca, Cruz Azul y América

articles.body: Pumas tiene su refuerzo para suplir la baja de Sebastián Córdova, fuera todo el torneo por lesión, y uno es un fichaje cualquiera para el equipo que hoy dirige Esteban Solari. Se trata de César Huerta, el último gran ídolo de la afición universitaria el que regresa desde el Anderlecht en un momento complicado para el club tras perder la final del torneo anterior ante Cruz Azul y la salida de Efraín Juárez. Con información de Rodrigo Celorio, que cubre al Club Universidad Nacional para TUDN, y de César Luis Merlo, especializado en fichajes, el acuerdo existe entre clubes y jugador para llevar a cabo el traspaso. “Se trata de una compra definitiva y Huerta tendrá un contrato de tres años. Este miércoles llegará a la Ciudad de México para realizarse los exámenes médicos de rigor y firmar con los universitarios”, comparte Merlo en Superdeportivo. Chino Huerta emigró en enero de 2025 al equipo de Bélgica, donde poco a poco fue perdiendo protagonismo, en parte también por las lesiones. Su venta a Europa fue por 2 millones de euros. El regreso de Huerta a la Liga MX se da con un equipo que no había sonado entre los rumores de su regreso desde Europa, ya que se mencionó con más fuerza al Toluca. Después del equipo de Antonio Mohamed, también se nombró a Cruz Azul y, en menor medida al América, ante la falta de refuerzos, pero los de la UNAM tendría de vuelta al jugador en Ciudad Universitaria. De acuerdo con información de DH Les Sports en Bélgica, Chino Huerta se rehusaba a regresar a México, pero cuando Pumas apareció en el panorama, comenzó a cambiar de idea. Los universitarios han conseguido 8 de 15 puntos disputados en las primeras cinco jornada del Apertura 2026 y se coloca en la posición 9 de la tabla, mientras que en la Leagues Cup quedó eliminado en la primera ronda.

articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is fast approaching and the Yahoo Fantasy Ultra Playbook has everything you need to know to before your draft, giving you the tools and analysis to crush the competition. Among that analysis is Joel Smyth's RB player profiles. Below is a sneak peek of some of the 25+ rusher profiles in the Ultra Playbook, including a ceiling and risk meter for each. If you subscribe to Ultra, there are nearly 150 player profiles to digest.

Get a free preview of what Ultra subscribers get with The Playbook, including a snapshot of our sleepers, breakouts, strategy tips, player profiles and more, right here.

Ceiling: If things fall in their favor, how big can they hit in 2026?

Risk: A subjective ranking based on injuries, surrounding injuries, coaching changes, how proven a player is, age, and other factors that bring on uncertainty

It's night and day for Kenneth Walker III in terms of his fantasy situation. He goes from an offense with a split backfield, and little work in the red zone, to a team whose offense is both high-scoring and lacking weapons. His contract and competition makes predicting top-12 RB volume reasonable, with opportunities in the red zone and passing game being key additions.

The fantasy obstacle for Walker has always been injuries. Although he's only missed 10 of 72 career games, only 41 of those games have come with 15+ touches due to leaving early, snap counts and coaching decisions. The 23.4 fantasy PPG in the NFL Playoffs last season is what fantasy managers hope will be what sticks from 2025. After the failed Isiah Pacheco-Kareem Hunt experiment, Andy Reid will look to go back to having a workhorse in Walker.

Can Daniel Jones come back strong? Taylor's production fell off after his quarterback's Achilles injury in 2025, production that started out as part of the No. 1 scoring offense in the NFL with a run-first mentality. JT is the definition of a bellcow RB, with underrated, career-high usage in the passing game last season. If Jones' injury causes less QB red-zone rushing and more checkdowns, Taylor could top his 2025 season easily as long as the offense can remain clicking. As one of only four running backs to be an RB1 in three consecutive seasons, he should be in for another RB1 season with high volume.

Before the J.K. Dobbins injury, the Broncos' rookie RB only handled 24% of RB carries last season. He was a TD machine that broke out in the second half of the season as the starter, although it diminished after Week 17 (the fantasy championship in most leagues). The return of Dobbins and addition of fourth-round pick Jonah Coleman makes it a more difficult path for Harvey to return to his peak. The offensive line and receiving opportunity are great, but the Broncos RB will just need to develop after a rookie season that was shaky in efficiency.

The concern is obvious: Henderson barely played in the NFL playoffs when it matters most. Four total snaps in the AFC Championship is #notgood. He is a big "if" player. If he gets 50% of the volume, that alone can be enough. If he gets 65%+ he can be a league winner. We saw it in spurts with three different top-five RB weeks alone, specifically posting RB1 numbers in his month without Rhamondre Stevenson, at 20 touches a week. His overall rushing efficiency and pass protection were sub-par, but it was his rookie season after all. If he can flirt with 15 touches per game, that'll be plenty to hit ADP in a New England offense.

Rumors of a running back by committee can hurt Pollard in a big way. Surprisingly, the Titans RB is one of three RBs to have 275+ carries in three straight seasons. Although he was relevantly efficient in 2025, the Tennessee offense held him back from any real fantasy payout. However, he has been a top-30 RB in each of the last four seasons, and should make it five if the Titans offense improves after overhauling that side of the ball.

Ben Johnson running backs have scored more than any since 2022, but Swift's production, especially in the second half of the season, surprisingly was limited to the ground game. He tied his career high in goal-line attempts but averaged a career low in targets. With Kyle Monangai increasing his workload later in the year, Swift should be an RB2 thanks to an elite rushing attack, yet with a lower ceiling compared to past seasons.

Nobody had a better offseason than 2025 fourth-rounder Bhayshul Tuten. After rumors of adding a top running back in the draft or free agency, the Jacksonville Jaguars replaced Travis Etienne Jr. with career backup Chris Rodriguez Jr. and passed on the position with all 10 of their NFL Draft selections. The volume is the X-Factor and the unknown.

If Jacksonville does use Tuten as a true 1A, he can be the biggest fantasy value in the draft. Tuten and Rodriguez both have the same strengths as inside runners and were dominant at the goal line in 2025. When it comes to receiving, Tuten has the clear advantage, although he was far behind Etienne in that department last season. With a top offense to support him and playcaller Liam Coen having the fifth-most RB fantasy points the last two seasons, Tuten is a high-upside target.

Warren is a reliable fantasy option that isn't always the most exciting draft-day selection. His efficiency has always been high, with the volume being the main eluding factor. In the Aaron Rodgers offense, RBs score plenty with a vast amount of targets available. Based on targets per route and yards per route, no RB was more efficient than Warren in 2025. Now that he's back healthy and without Kenny Gainwell, that passing involvement could be the key to fantasy success if he can beat out Rico Dowdle for that primary role.

articles.title: College sports' eligibility crisis is sprawling well beyond LSU, football and basketball — 'It's beyond unfair. It's heartless.'
articles.summary: While some players who previously signed contracts in the NFL or NBA have been able to win state court rulings to return to college, others have been left in...
articles.body:
On Friday, the day he was scheduled to fly to Knoxville, Tennessee, to begin camp as a late addition to the Volunteers, Monty Hunt awoke in his San Diego home to a text.

A Tennessee staff member informed him that he was, as of that morning, no longer eligible.

How could he be eligible one day and not eligible another?

Upon opening social media, he got his answer: A federal appeals court ruled in favor of the NCAA by freezing a Colorado court's sweeping decision to grant all of the 2022 high school class members an additional fifth year of eligibility.

The appeals decision — to stay the lower court's order until the completion of a full appeals process — means that Hunt's lifelong dream, at least for now, is dashed. And so too is the $50,000 in promised NIL compensation and scholarship costs.

"It's stressful for sure," he told Yahoo Sports on Monday during an interview. "I was waiting all these months and I finally got a chance to play SEC ball and the day before I leave, it gets pulled."

The appeals court ruling dealt a stunning blow to hundreds of athletes across the college sports landscape who were preparing to play this fall season in their respective sport through the federal ruling out of Colorado.

They were actively practicing, some even had already participated in exhibition games. They were on depth charts, travel rosters, scholarship lists and even NIL payment plans. They are team captains, key backups and role players.

Out from under them all, the proverbial rug was pulled.

"I literally spent all day Friday crying," said Ocean Rideout, a Portland State soccer player.

In the middle of a multi-game exhibition trip to California last week, Rideout learned of the court's ruling from an assistant coach at breakfast, just a few hours after she started in a preseason match and hours before she was scheduled to start in another one.

"I was suspended from all team activities," she said. "It's emotionally distressing to be in a limbo situation. One day you are eligible and one day you are ineligible."

Like many athletes across the country, Rideout spent much of her weekend researching ways to file a lawsuit in state court to regain her eligibility. It beats waiting weeks or months for the completion of an appeals process in the federal case in Colorado.

College administrators and athletes say that's the biggest rub with all of this: Inconsistent judicial decisions create an uneven playing field.

Those athletes who did not file or win lawsuits in state court are at the mercy of the Colorado federal case. A mad scramble is now unfolding for athletes to file locally.

Most of these players are similarly situated as part of the 2022 high school class requesting a fifth season of eligibility — a move sparked by the NCAA's new eligibility policy to grant athletes the ability to play five seasons, not four as was the case under the previous policy. However, the NCAA — a membership association where schools create the rules — did not grant an exception to those four-year players graduating this spring.

With the sweeping federal, class-action ruling frozen, hundreds of athletes are now exploring state-wide lawsuits — at least those who can afford it.

"I'm trying to find an attorney that will do it pro bono," Rideout said. "I don't have NIL funds like some of the football players."

Some may be unable to do so, like Abby Jeffries, a track and field athlete at Long Island University. As a named plaintiff in the federal case, she is unlikely to win an individual state court lawsuit, her attorneys say.

"It's beyond unfair. It's heartless," Jeffries said of the NCAA's approach.

"What happened with the stay has been devastating to athletes all over the country," said Diana Florence, with Shumaker, Loop & Kendrick law firm and one of the leaders of a team of attorneys representing athletes in the Colorado federal case. "If these athletes were born one year later, they'd be greeted with open arms for next year's eligibility. The NCAA's mission is supposed to center on the best interest of the student athlete. In what way is preventing athletes like Abby Jeffries from competing consistent with that mission?"

The Colorado ruling sent Jeffries, an aspiring medical student, quite literally to the bank. She needed to extract a $30,000 loan now to cover tuition after her scholarship was revoked.

"It's a mess," said Darren Heitner, a Florida-based sports law attorney who claims he's received nearly 1,000 inquiries since Friday's ruling. He expects dozens of lawsuits to be filed this week from athletes seeking a fifth season of eligibility.

More than 18 eligibility lawsuits have already been filed in 15 different states by more than 150 athletes in response to the association not making an exception for those 2022 high school class members. The NCAA has won a stay in three: the federal court decision, one in Ohio and another in New Jersey.

No single suit has drawn more attention than a Louisiana judge's decision to grant a group of athletes a fifth year, including several of them who signed NFL undrafted free agent contracts and even competed in NFL preseason games.

At least two of those players hold agreements to join coach Lane Kiffin and the LSU football team: tight end Dae'Quan Wright from the Cleveland Browns and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris from the New Orleans Saints . Kiffin coached both last year at Ole Miss.

Though he was careful not to confirm any new signings, Kiffin addressed the situation during a regularly scheduled news conference on Monday, defending his program and other schools for recruiting players in the NFL. He pointed the finger at the current system .

Athletes are only using legal avenues to regain eligibility that they did not know would exist, he said. The NCAA did not vote to implement the new five-year eligibility policy until June. Many players were required to make the decision to turn professional months before that.

"Because of the [court] rulings, they are going to play for you or someone else," Kiffin said. "We made the decision to recruit them. It's wrong to be critical of these kids. They were granted a fifth year and a judge said they were wronged."

But his own conference is taking exception to his transactional moves.

Many players choose to file legally knowing they have an open roster spot at a specific school or schools. This often means that schools are supporting player lawsuits that are challenging the very rules that the schools themselves created.

In a hurriedly called virtual SEC presidents meeting on Monday night, the league's leaders unanimously supported opposition to professional players returning to college, even releasing a statement decrying such.

"College sports are for college athletes," one of the lines of the statement read.

Beyond the statement, university presidents and league officials are expected to direct their athletic departments against accepting players who signed professional contracts and competed in pro contests, or risk potential sanctions, according to those with knowledge of the meeting.

According to SEC bylaws, commissioner Greg Sankey and/or the conference's presidents hold authority to deem a player ineligible, fine or suspend school coaches and administrators, and even prohibit a program from competing in league games or the conference championship.

More discussion on these topics are expected during a joint, two-day meeting of SEC presidents and athletic directors in Birmingham that begins Tuesday — an unusual and significant gathering that was scheduled weeks ago, where officials plan to continue exploring a long-discussed conference-only governance model .

The eligibility fiasco is now expected to take center stage at a meeting that could turn tense and even heated.

LSU's new president, Wade Rousse, and athletic director, Verge Ausberry, are scheduled to attend. The program not only is in line to accept multiple professional football players. Men's basketball head coach Will Wade landed a big win Monday night: A Louisiana judge granted additional eligibility for RJ Luis to return to college . Luis, a member of the 2022 high school class, went undrafted during the 2025 NBA Draft, signed a two-way contract with the Utah Jazz, was traded to the Boston Celtics and played in three NBA games.

Awaiting Luis following the victory was none other than Wade, who embraced the player outside of the court room in an emotional moment caught by a local TV sports anchor from WBRZ. Wade landed a key piece for the inaugural team of his second stint in Baton Rouge.

Outside the courthouse in Baton Rouge on Monday, Luis' attorney, Elliot Abrams, described the NCAA's decision to permit schools to pay players directly as creating a "professional league," where "arbitrary" eligibility rules "don't stand up to reason."

"This is a judge forcing the NCAA to live up to the law," he told reporters.

During an interview on Monday, one college sports stakeholder described the situation as Sankey's "Sorsby moment," a reference to Brendan Sorsby and Texas Tech's legal entanglement with the Big 12. The conference filed suit against the school for its intentions to play a player who gambled on his own team.

If the SEC penalizes LSU or the professional athletes who plan to play there, will the school or those athletes file suit against the conference? Will the league file suit against its own school?

LSU may be aggressively signing these players at a higher clip than most, but the school isn't alone. In fact, just last week, a former Kentucky basketball player, Mark Mitchell, won a lawsuit for additional eligibility and is transferring to Missouri . This flies directly in the face of another SEC policy against intraconference transfers outside of the portal period.

On Monday, attorneys filed a motion to expedite the federal case in Colorado.

The goal: reach some sort of conclusion before the start of, or at least during, the fall sports season. It may be difficult. Football season kicks off this weekend.

The expedited motion is in an attempt to schedule oral arguments on the court's September calendar. If the judge declines or the calendar is full, that puts the case on the November calendar.

"We are doing everything we can to accelerate the briefing," said Rob Shelquist, another attorney on the case from Cuneo Gilbert Flannery & LaDuca. "If this drags to November, it is probably the end of the road for the fall athletes. If the court doesn't accelerate briefing and this languishes until November, we will still do everything we can to save the winter and spring athletes. The NCAA claims its mission is to create opportunities for athletes and yet we are the ones fighting to allow schools and coaches who want to fill open roster spots and award unused scholarships to these athletes."

Meanwhile, the inequalities will continue across the landscape.

For instance, Texas State has a football player on its roster, linebacker Treylin Payne, who's now ineligible after the Colorado decision. The Bobcats' season-opening opponent, Texas, will play in the game lineman Cole Hutson , who participated in minicamps with the Browns and Cowboys before winning a local eligibility lawsuit.

The players are in a similar situation as 2022 high school athletes seeking a fifth season of eligibility. Payne is expected, like so many others, to seek a state court ruling.

Yahoo Sports introduces a new era with College Fantasy Football: Sign up and get ready to play!

Sean McVay can't comprehend players going from NFL camps back to college: 'I feel like I took a freakin' gummy'

Akron announces its 'Offensive Coordinator of the Game,' who will help Joe Moorhead script opening drive vs. Robert Morris

Coaches have publicly expressed varying degrees of opinions on the situation.

Some, like Oregon 's Dan Lanning, rebuff the notion of recruiting pro players.

"Once you go to the NFL, to me, you're in the NFL. You don't get the opportunity to come back," Lanning said.

But others, like Ohio State's Ryan Day, suggested that he'd consider NFL players who formerly played who are granted eligibility. "Do I like anything about it? Absolutely not, but we gotta do what's right for Ohio State," Day said.

Meanwhile, NCAA executives and the power conference commissioners continue to hold conversations on their approach and options. There is no easy solution for the situation, administrators say, but there are several options to consider.

Leaders could issue a broad waiver to grant all members of the 2022 high school class eligibility, but that likely means creating a transfer portal for movement and exceptions for roster caps. Those are moves that school executives declined to make in May — a reason that an exception wasn't made to begin with.

This move also does not solve another festering problem for college officials: the ban on professional players returning to college, which is now under attack within these eligibility lawsuits.

Leaders could decide to continue to litigate individual state and federal court cases, hoping for more friendly judicial decisions or appeals court victories like the one in Colorado. But this is costly, time-consuming and creates the current uneven playing field.

Another option has emerged, too: conferences taking matters into their own hands by creating league policies and enforcing them from the conference office. This dovetails with this week's meetings in Birmingham as leaders consider and view presentations of league-wide governance in an effort to limit the amount of legal challenges.

In fact, all four power leagues are expected to consider such a rule — something that may put the conferences at the center of new lawsuits, rather than the NCAA.

In the meantime, it isn't just football and basketball players chasing hundreds of thousands of dollars who are caught in the quagmire. Soccer, field hockey and track athletes are mired in what one person calls the "NCAA Trap."

"It's beyond unfair," said Jeffries, the track athlete at Long Island who now needs a bank loan to enroll in classes. "My coaches told me, 'We have the [scholarship] money for you! We just can't do it!'"

articles.title: Afcon 2028: Ethiopia submits official bid to host tournament in East Africa
articles.summary: Ethiopia submits a bid to host the 2028 Africa Cup of Nations despite lacking enough stadiums to host a 24-team tournament.
articles.body:
Ethiopia has submitted an official bid to host the 2028 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon).

The country's football federation (EFF) says its government-backed proposal affirms "the nation's full readiness to host Africa's biggest footballing event".

Ethiopia has staged Afcon three times, in 1962, 1968 and 1976, but its footballing infrastructure lags well behind others on the continent.

The nation had just one stadium approved for use by the Confederation of African Football (Caf) last season but is in the process of inaugurating a new international stadium and sports complex in Addis Ababa.

That venue in the capital could provide one location for the tournament, but whether Ethiopia has enough compliant venues to host a 24-team Afcon across multiple locations remains a major question.

A number of existing regional facilities are understood not to meet Fifa or Caf standards in terms of infrastructure, facilities and overall match-day requirements.

Ethiopia played its home qualifiers for the 2026 Fifa World Cup at neutral venues in Morocco and Rwanda but did host matches in Dire Dawa earlier this year.

Last month, Caf president Patrice Motsepe said his organisation had received "exciting bids" for the 2028, 2032 and 2036 Afcons - with the tournament set to move to a four-year cycle after 2028 .

Botswana, Namibia, South Africa and Zimbabwe announced a joint Southern African bid for the 2028 finals earlier this year.

Despite reports that Morocco - hosts of the 2025 edition - could stage the tournament again in two years' time, BBC Sport Africa understands the kingdom is not in the running and instead is focusing on preparations to co-host the 2030 Fifa World Cup.

Meanwhile, Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger - three countries led by military governments - have expressed interest in co-hosting in 2032.

The 2027 Afcon is scheduled to take place in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from 19 June to 17 July next year, with the competition returning to East Africa for the first time since it was held in Ethiopia in 1976.

Ethiopia won the Afcon title on home soil in 1962 but the Walia Ibex, ranked 143rd in the world and 43rd in Africa, have only qualified for the tournament three times since they last hosted.

Their most recent appearance came at the 2021 edition, when they finished bottom without a win in a group containing Cameroon, Burkina Faso and Cape Verde.

Ethiopia beat Sao Tome and Principe in the preliminary round of qualifiers for next year's Afcon and have been drawn alongside Senegal, Mozambique and Sudan in Group J.

Is holding Afcon every four years 'totally wrong' or 'good call'? Published 22 January

Is holding Afcon every four years 'totally wrong' or 'good call'?

The EFF's announcement that it wants to host Afcon has generated mixed reactions, with critics questioning whether the country is truly prepared to host a tournament of this scale.

Ethiopia was one of just three nations to play at the first Afcon in 1957, but the 52,000-seat Bahir Dar Stadium in the north of the country is currently the only facility it posseses which is approved by Caf.

Meanwhile, the 62,000-capacity Adey Abeba International Stadium in Addis Ababa is expected to be completed next year.

Three other proposed stadiums are at much earlier stages of development and would need significant work to meet Caf's requirements in time for 2028.

However, hosting Afcon would require more than upgrading or constructing stadiums. The country would also need adequate training facilities, gyms, accommodation and entertainment venues, as well as reliable urban transport and security infrastructure.

Security is a major concern for Ethiopia's bid. Although the capital city is comparatively safe, several parts of the country continue to experience armed conflict, political unrest and other security challenges.

Addressing these concerns, alongside the infrastructure requirements, would be critical if Ethiopia is to successfully host Afcon 2028.

articles.title: Infantino’s presidency under threat: FIFA elections, challengers, dates
articles.summary: Amid waning support and growing criticism, the FIFA chief looks to hold onto his powerful position in world football.
articles.body:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino, currently the most powerful man in world football, appears to be pulling out all the stops in a bid to retain his position despite growing calls for his ouster and wide-ranging disapproval of his plans.

The 56-year-old has been in charge of FIFA for over 10 years and is seen as a divisive figure in international football, with his close ties to some of the most powerful global leaders and plans for maximising revenue from football viewed as a threat to the game.

list 2 of 4 Big-spending Tottenham sign Brazilian winger Savinho from Manchester City

list 3 of 4 Ex-Wimbledon champion Vondrousova appeals to CAS over four-year doping ban

list 4 of 4 Ex-Liverpool star Fabinho reunited with Mohamed Salah at Trabzonspor

With a little over six months until the next round of elections for FIFA’s presidency, Infantino appears to be losing ground among his usual backers in national football federations and regional confederations.

Here’s a look at where Infantino stands in terms of support and what challenges lie ahead for him and FIFA:

Why is Infantino being challenged as FIFA president?

While the Swiss head of FIFA has never been a widely popular figure with football fans, he has enjoyed support amongst leading figures in the sport and global leaders.

This popularity, however, has waned over the past few months, especially since making no secret of his close ties with United States President Donald Trump and announcing FIFA’s plans to privatise the World Cup in order to maximise revenue from the tournament.

The FIFA chief first met Trump at the White House in 2018 after the US was awarded the co-hosting rights to the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Infantino has since made several public appearances with the US president, including at the so-called Summit for Peace in Egypt in October 2025.

Infantino was the target of widespread scathing criticism in December, when he handed the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize to the US president at the FIFA World Cup 2026 draw held at the Kennedy Centre in Washington, DC.

The final blow to the global football chief’s position came in the days after the World Cup, when he invited private investors to buy a stake in future profits from World Cups and all FIFA events. The investor group was led by Joshua Kushner , an American businessman who is also the younger brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

While the ensuing backlash – which included pledges by European nations to boycott FIFA events and claims from senior staff that Infantino deceived everyone – led Infantino to announce Friday that he was abandoning the plan , irreparable damage had already been to his reputation.

He now faces a race against time to garner support in his push for an extraordinary fourth term as president.

How many terms can one FIFA president have?

FIFA presidents are limited to three terms in office, with each term lasting four years.

However, in 2022, Infantino successfully argued that his first spell in charge, which began when he was elected at an extraordinary FIFA Congress ⁠in 2016 following Sepp Blatter’s resignation, should not count towards that limit because it completed an interrupted mandate.

His plans to run for a fourth term have been questioned by critics and rights groups, who have asked FIFA’s Governance, Audit and Compliance Committee (GACC) to block Infantino’s re-election bid.

What are the key dates for FIFA elections and how do they work?

The polls to elect FIFA’s next president will be held at the global governing body’s next congress, which is slated for March 18, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco.

All challengers vying for the post must declare their candidacy by November 18.

The candidates will face off in a poll involving all 211 FIFA member nations, with 106 votes required to pick a winner.

Who are the likely candidates to challenge Infantino for the FIFA presidency?

European football (UEFA) chief Aleksander Ceferin has ruled himself out from the running and no individuals have announced their plans to challenge Infantino openly.

However, a number of regional FIFA confederation chiefs and some other powerful figures in global football have been tipped as potential candidates . They are:

Victor Montagliani, president of the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF)

Nasser al-Khelaifi, chairman of the European Club Association (ECA) and president of Paris Saint Germain football club

Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa, president of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC)

Patrice Motsepe, president of the Confederation of African Football (CAF)

How has Infantino reacted to the challenge?

The FIFA chief has been scrambling to gather support and has made public appearances despite having being advised to maintain a low profile. He was asked by Montagliani to skip an Under-14 football event in the Caribbean last week but Infantino posted photos on his Instagram account, showing his meeting with political and football officials from the Dominican Republic.

The move was seen as an attempt to seek support from the regional football officials, but a FIFA statement quoted Infantino as saying: “It’s important to engage, to have a dialogue, to express views and opinions – a lot [has] been happening in the last few weeks and it’s important that you hear, you listen and you’re able to, also, express what your feelings are.”

Infantino’s latest public appearance was in France on Monday, where he attended the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup at the Grand Palais in Paris and was seated besides French President Emmanuel Macron and the Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia Mohammed bin Salman.

Which national football federations and regional confederations are backing Infantino?

Despite the ongoing crisis, Infantino has found longstanding support from the African confederation , with CAF’s top decision-making body late siding with the ⁠FIFA president.

Mexico and Argentina have also put their weight behind him, with South America’s CONMEBOL football governing body issuing a statement this month to reject any attempt to oust Infantino that did not involve a vote of all 211 members.

The FIFA Under-20 Women’s World Cup is less than two weeks away, with the tournament kicking off on September 5 in Poland.

While UEFA issued a statement earlier this month saying its 55-member association remains committed to boycotting FIFA competitions, the competition is slated to go ahead as scheduled.

articles.title: Xavi, en su presentación: "Quiero que mi Países Bajos tenga el balón, soy un ganador"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador español fue presentado oficialmente por la Federación neerlandesa
articles.summary: El entrenador español fue presentado oficialmente por la Federación neerlandesa
articles.body: Xavi Hernández (XH) fue presentado oficialmente por la Federación de Países Bajos como su nuevo seleccionador hasta el Mundial 2030. En una multitudinaria rueda de Prensa, XH compareció junto al director deportivo de la Federación, el exmundialista Nigel de Jong. Xavi se expresó en español e inglés y afrontó la rueda de Prensa con traductor al neerlandés y aceptando las preguntas de los numerosos medios que allí había.   Sus primeros deseos: "Tengo muchas conexiones con este país. La sensación es que voy a la Universidad del Fútbol. Quiero que mi Selección siempre tenga el balón, pero con pasión. Estamos aquí para competir, disfrutar y ganar. E insisto: estamos aquí para ganar". El Barça: "Estar allí fue un máster, tanto para lo bueno como para lo menos bueno. Nos nutrimos muchísimo en Can Barça del fútbol de Países Bajos y ahora es una oportunidad de devolver todo aquí". Su sistema de juego: "Sé que Van Gaal o Koeman han jugado con cinco defensas atrás. Pero ésa no es mi idea para mi equipo. Yo quiero jugar con otros sistemas: 4-3-3, 4-2-3-1 o 3-4-3. Creo que podemos dominar mejor el juego con estos sistemas".  De Jong (Barça): "Frenkie está muy motivado con nuestro fichaje. Lo primero es que ojalá se pueda recuperar bien y lo antes posible, pues es un jugador muy importante para todos". Un ganador: "Sé que soy un seleccionador extranjero. Pero estoy aquí para ayudar a la Federación, al staff y a los jugadores. Quiero ganar. Siento la presión, pero soy un ganador, y estoy listo, súperlisto". Cruyff: "¿Qué aprendí de Johan? En las etapas finales de su vida hablé mucho con él, incluso cuando estaba enfermo. Y siempre fue muy positivo, también cuando estaba enfermo. Aprendí eso. Siempre sonriendo, vibras positivas. Esto es lo que voy a mostrar a mis jugadores. Disfrutemos el proceso, y entonces estaremos más cerca de Cruyff". El citado Nigel de Jong, director deportivo de Países Bajos, confirmó esto: "Nuestro primer candidato para reemplazar a Ronald Koeman fue Pep Guardiola, pero él quería tomarse un año de descanso. Nuestro segundo candidato fue Arne Slot (no tiene equipo), pero él prefirió seguir activo en el fútbol de clubes. Luego pasamos al tercer candidato, el hombre a mi lado, Xavi Hernández".

articles.title: Carlos Baleba: Manchester United sign Cameroon midfielder from Brighton in £70m deal
articles.summary: Manchester United sign Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton in a £70m deal.
articles.body:
Manchester United have signed Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton in a £70m deal.

The Old Trafford club have paid an initial £65m, plus a potential £5m in add-ons, for the 22-year-old, while Brighton have negotiated a sell-on clause.

United targeted Baleba after deciding to strengthen their midfield further following the summer arrivals of Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa .

Baleba has signed a five year-contract at Old Trafford, with the option to extend for a further year.

"It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams," he said. "Playing at Old Trafford is always special, but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

"I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick. His experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

"The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together."

Baleba's move follows United's shock 2-0 defeat by Hull City in Saturday's Premier League opener, where Santos and Tielemans made their midfield debuts.

United reignited their interest after attempting to sign him last year near deadline day, but were put off by Brighton 's valuation, which was in excess of £100m.

Baleba, who joined Brighton from Lille in 2023, is currently sidelined with an ankle injury he picked up during the Seagulls' pre-season training camp in Austria.

He made 112 appearances for Brighton , scoring four times, and 31 in the Premier League last season as they finished eighth to qualify for this season's Conference League.

"Last season was hard," admitted Baleba in a farewell video.

"There was a night against Aston Villa when I came off after 22 minutes. I sat in the dugout and could not lift my head up. You did not boo me. I have thought about that more than you know. You had every reason to and you did not.

"I will be looking for your result every week for the rest of my life. Thank you, Brighton fans."

The move has taken United's summer spending up to £153m as they prepare for a return to the Champions League for the first time since the 2023-24 campaign.

"[He is] a huge talent that the club has been trying to follow for a long time." Red Devils captain Bruno Fernandes told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Someone that can improve our team and has different qualities to what we already have in the club.

"The expectation is very high but also we know he is a player we need to give time to become an even better version of himself. We are here to help him set [in] as quick as possible and to help us win games."

What does your Premier League club still need in the transfer window? Published 11 hours ago

What does your Premier League club still need in the transfer window?

United will hope for the 2024-25 version of Baleba rather than last season's because it was his performances in that campaign that attracted them.

We can't know what would have happened if the approach for Mateus Fernandes had been successful, nor if Mason Mount had not suffered the injury in the pre-season game with Paris St-Germain two weeks ago that ruled him out of the Premier League opener.

However, even before Saturday's disappointing loss at Hull it is clear that, despite adding Santos and Tielemans to their midfield ranks, they still lack physicality and power.

In theory, Baleba should solve that issue.

The 22-year-old is strong in possession, covers ground quickly, is good in the air and alert to danger.

Crucially, he also has three years' worth of top-flight experience in England behind him, having moved to Brighton from Lille when he was 19. It gives him the edge on Santos, also 22, and it will be interesting to see whether the pair compete for the same place at the base of Michael Carrick's midfield or if, against the best sides, they might play together.

It will also be fascinating to see if he gets asked to fill in at left-back too.

He has played there before and, unlike Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui - who could also switch sides if Luke Shaw is unavailable - is left-footed.

Paul Pogba is the only midfield player United have signed for more than the £70m they are committing to Baleba which, given his age, is a statement in itself.

'Baleba complements United's other midfielders'

Baleba's appeal lies less in creativity and more in his ability to win possession, cover ground and then carry his team forward.

His 2025-26 campaign was quieter than the previous one, but his 2024-25 numbers show why United have tracked him for so long. He ranked fourth among Premier League midfielders for possessions won in the middle third (107) and interceptions (46), was fifth for ball recoveries (197) and seventh for duels won (199).

That defensive output was matched by his ability to progress possession himself.

Baleba averaged 6.7 progressive carries per 90 minutes, with only three qualifying Premier League defensive midfielders recording more, while 2.9 of those carries travelled at least 10 metres.

His athleticism underpins that game as he reached a top speed of 34.5km/h in 2024-25, compared with 30.5km/h for Casemiro, and averaged 8.2 defensive actions per 90.

He is not necessarily the midfielder United would rely on to dictate possession. Only 11.8% of his passes were classed as line-breaking that season and 22.7% travelled forward - both below the average for central and defensive midfielders.

But that may make him complementary to United's other options rather than a direct alternative. Tielemans can provide more of the progressive distribution, while Baleba offers defensive security and the ability to drive through midfield.

Alongside Kobbie Mainoo, he could take on more of the ball-winning and ground-covering work, while a partnership with Santos could allow Baleba greater freedom to operate box to box.

That versatility is reflected in his positioning as he spent 88% of his minutes last season as a defensive midfielder and 12% in central midfield, suggesting he can anchor the side or step forward depending on who plays alongside him.

United most commonly defended in a 4-2-2-2 last season under Carrick, accounting for 55.9% of their out-of-possession shapes. Baleba's dynamism could be especially valuable in a system where central midfielders are asked to defend large spaces and stop counter-attacks.

There may, however, be an adaptation period.

Baleba is recovering from an ankle ligament injury suffered in pre-season and will need time to recover his match sharpness.

United have also looked to spend longer spells in possession under Carrick, progressing through midfield with quick combinations. Baleba's game is better suited to more open contests, but his passing profile suggests he may need time to adjust to greater responsibility in build-up.

His left foot and mobility should still make him a natural partner for players such as Tielemans or Bruno Fernandes. There is development ahead of him at 22, not least after last season's dip, but at his best Baleba combines defensive activity with the acceleration and carrying power to transform a turnover into an attack within seconds.

articles.title: Bold College Fantasy Football predictions for the 2026 season
articles.summary: Will these six bold college fantasy football predictions come true?
articles.body:
With college football mercifully starting back up this weekend, we will finally get to see how these newly constructed rosters perform in reality as opposed to in theory. Since Yahoo College Fantasy drafts are in full swing, it's time to break out some bold CFF-oriented predictions for the 2026 season.

Jadan Baugh leads the nation in rushing yardage

A powerful-yet-graceful Man Beast, Baugh is 6'1"/228 pounds, squats 565 pounds and has a 4.57 40 speed. He was held back by the hapless Billy Napier last season but managed to score 17+ fantasy points in his last six contests following Napier's dismissal. New Florida head coach Jon Sumrall is well-known for his affinity of using his primary running back as a bell cow, as is evidenced by his prolific usage of Kimani Vidal back at Troy, with Vidal leading the entire nation in rushing under Sumrall's tutelage.

I think Sumrall unleashes Baugh on the SEC, to devastating effect, with the future top-50 NFL Draft pick finally emerging as the star he was destined to be. Baugh is a major priority for me and well worth a first-round fantasy draft selection with the workload he is projected to receive.

Jayden 'Duke' Scott takes the ACC by storm and averages 20 Fantasy PPG

Scott averaged 6.1 yards per touch with a pristine 94% catch rate as Hollywood Smothers' backup last year, and inherits the Wolfpack's starting gig heading into the season. The numbers were recounted in the indispensable Feldman Freaks List , with Scott reportedly running a 4.35s 40-yard dash while squatting 575 lbs with 20 bench reps. Those are rare numbers for a 5'10/235-pounder and well beyond what Smothers is capable of. NC State dodges Miami, Clemson and Notre Dame (honorary ACC member), leaving Scott to feast on the soft underbelly of the ACC. I think Scott clears the elite 20-PPG mark and goes on to have a top-10 College Fantasy campaign.

Ryan Coleman-Williams is a top-five scoring wide receiver

The uncomfortable truth is that Coleman-Williams' 10 drops sabotaged critical opportunities and turned a promising sophomore season into a disappointment. The talent did not vanish; he still averaged 6.8 yards after the catch, showing the same acceleration and open-field creativity that powered his freshman breakout. Now that explosive sophomore QB Keelon Russell has secured the starting job, Coleman-Williams has an Elite-11-winning signal-caller to work with.

Alabama's most difficult defensive test all season comes Oct. 11 versus Georgia, with the remainder of the schedule being very favorable from a fantasy perspective. The news out of camp is that RCW has regained his freshman magic when he reclassified as a 17-year-old in order to play in 2024. I think Coleman-Williams will correct the case of the yips he had in 2025 and ascend back into the upper crust of P4 wide receivers, finishing as a top-five scorer at the position.

Jamal Roberts finishes as a top-15 CFF running back

One of the most important contingency backs in fantasy football after averaging 6.17 yards per carry, Roberts also caught 17 passes for 139 yards and averaged 10.51 per game despite being a backup. Roberts' emergence as a quality RB2 averaging 0.97 fantasy points per touch shows he can support Missouri's offense if asked to lead it, and with breaking news indicating Ahmad Hardy is set to miss at least the first game, we could have a situation where the unfortunate gunshot victim is held back for most of the season until he is completely healthy in order to protect his NFL Draft stock.

Play Yahoo's new College Fantasy Football game: Create or join a league now!

I think Roberts gets the full workload for a Mizzou squad that averaged 228 rushing yards per game last season and returns three starters on a devastating offensive line that boasts 118 total career line starts. Whoever gets that starting job is going to produce, full stop, and I think that player is Roberts.

Omarion Miller takes the WR1 job at ASU and is a top-10 fantasy wideout

I'm a longtime fan of BC-to-ASU transfer WR Reed Harris and his ability to win downfield on the boundary. However, after watching Miller it became clear that he is simply operating at a different level and is deserving of Jordyn Tyson's high volume, alpha-WR1 role in Kenny Dillingham's offense.

Miller came on strong in his final seven games, accruing 608 of his 808 yards and 32 of his 45 receptions, as he took over the Buffs' receiving room while cashing in seven touchdowns over that span. His 34% deep target rate and 3.4 fantasy points per touch average foreshadows a massive leap in production now that he has a proven offensive guru steering the ship. Imagine what Miller is capable of now that he's away from the Colorado circus, where QB JuJu Lewis said they were essentially winging it on offense last year with no real structure.

Miller is a league-winner who is somehow being selected in the Round 8-10 range in most Yahoo Standard Leagues.

Post-hype sleeper QB Nico Iamaleava tears up the Big Ten and averages 25 fantasy points per game

Iamleava was behind the 8-ball last year after transferring late in the cycle from Tennessee to UCLA in a contentious QB swap that sent UCLA signal-caller Joey Aguilar packing to Knoxville. To compound matters, former head coach Deshaun Foster was inarguably one of the worst P4 coaching hires of the last decade, leaving Iamleava without structure and direction. The Bruins brought in new head coach Bob Chesney from James Madison, where he took the Dukes to the CFP Playoff and guided QB Alonza Barnett to an excellent 23.8 fantasy PPG season.

Skillset-wise, Iamleava is essentially a souped-up version of Barnett and was the only returning quarterback in the Power Four who rushed for 400+ yards and failed to eclipse the 20 PPG threshold. As someone who attended several UCLA games over Foster's tenure, and was also present at the Bruins spring game, I can say with confidence that Chesney has completely changed the atmosphere around the program. With Chesney resetting the roster through the transfer portal in the same manner that his JMU predecessor Curt Cignetti did at Indiana, I think UCLA hits the ground running and instantly becomes a credible Big Ten program, with Nico emerging from the post-hype-sleeper doldrums to become a top-20 scoring quarterback and CFF weapon who clears the 25 PPG barrier.

articles.title: Man Utd transfer news: Will Michael Carrick's side buy a left-back before transfer window closes?
articles.summary: After spending £155m on three midfielders, now Manchester United must decide whether to try to buy a left-back
articles.body:
The signing of Carlos Baleba completes a £155m summer revamp of Manchester United's midfield.

At the end of last season, midfield was targeted as a priority area as United looked to build on qualification for the Champions League after a two-year absence.

Baleba arrives along with Andrey Santos, a £48m signing from Chelsea, and £35m former Aston Villa man Youri Tielemans.

It means that, along with England's Kobbie Mainoo, United now have a spread of different attributes across their four-man midfield, three of whom are 22 or younger.

But, at Manchester United, one bad result brings intense pressure.

Even Michael Carrick's calm exterior cracked in a post-match exchange with former Middlesbrough and Swindon Town forward Jan Aage Fjortoft, now a TV presenter for Viaplay, following the shock defeat at Hull when the Norwegian suggested there was a lack of passion in United's ranks.

"Come on, that's ridiculous," replied Carrick. "You played football. You understand. That's a ridiculous thing to say."

So, now the midfield is sorted, it is natural for fans to look at the other areas of Carrick's squad that could do with reinforcements; namely left-back.

Baleba completes £70m Man Utd move from Brighton Published 11 hours ago

Baleba completes £70m Man Utd move from Brighton

Signing an additional left-back has looked an obvious thing for Manchester United to do.

Luke Shaw started all 38 Premier League games last season. He started at Hull. Of United's past 44 league games, the 31-year-old England international has failed to start just one, the final game of the 2024-25 campaign, four days after the Europa League final defeat by Tottenham – and he went on the post-season tour of Asia immediately afterwards.

But, before that, Shaw's injury record had not been great.

Between February 2024 and April 2025, he played as many games for England (three) as he did for his club. He missed three months at the start of the 2023-24 campaign.

There were calf and hamstring issues but also a feeling Erik ten Hag rushed him back too quickly.

More than anyone, Shaw benefited from a 40-game season, allowing him to prepare properly, largely for one game a week, sometimes not even that.

That preparation time will not be repeated.

Although there are blank midweeks between Manchester United's first three games, if they get through two EFL Cup rounds, they will not have a full midweek without a game, other than during international breaks, until the one that includes Christmas Day.

It is the combination of Shaw's injury record and the crush of games that has led to the feeling another left-back will arrive.

There is no doubt the club like Newcastle's Lewis Hall. At 21, he is the right age profile and ideally suited to challenging Shaw for his place, with the safety net of there being enough games to keep both men happy.

However, Newcastle don't want to sell. It would take a huge offer to persuade them otherwise and Manchester United's powerbrokers have proved on numerous occasions this summer they will not be held to ransom, or overpay, for players.

In addition, how much money do they have to spend?

In published third-quarter financial accounts to 31 March, United confirmed they owed £405.75m in outstanding transfer fees, £171.14m of which was due after more than one year. The club are still to outline what the additional $125m (£91.64m) they borrowed in a wider refinancing announced in June will be used for.

The assumption is £70m for Baleba, equal the sum United paid for Casemiro in 2022 and a figure only exceeded in their history in terms of midfielders by the club record £89m spent on Paul Pogba, is at the top end of what they wanted to pay.

Plenty of alternative left-backs to Hall have been mentioned.

Racing Santander's 19-year-old Jorge Salinas has a €16m (£13.7m) release clause, but is also coveted by Atletico Madrid.

Barcelona's Alejandro Balde was left out of the 5-0 La Liga victory over Elche by coach Hansi Flick, to allow him to "clear his mind" amid intense transfer speculation, with United among those to be linked with the 22-year-old Spain international. Barcelona are said to value him between €30m (£25.66m) and €40m (£34.22m).

With a week to go before the transfer window closes, the situation is thought to be fluid, but caution in United circles around the expectations of a new left-back being signed is being stressed.

A significant sale could change the dynamic.

However, the idea of Marcus Rashford leaving has virtually been ruled out with confirmation he will wear the coveted number nine shirt this season, while the anticipated exit of Manuel Ugarte had to be scrapped when he was injured at the World Cup.

Of Carrick's senior squad, forward Joshua Zirkzee appears surplus to requirements, yet with fitness doubts over Amad Diallo – the club are choosing to offer no clarification on the extent of his injury amid a report he could be out for up to six weeks – it is uncertain whether interest from Serie A will lead to a sale.

Carrick does have options at left-back without bringing anyone else in. Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have both switched flanks in the past, while Baleba, a left-footed player, has played at full-back for Brighton previously.

In addition, Harry Amass was Shaw's back-up during pre-season and the 19-year-old remains at United. But he was not included in Carrick's squad for the Hull trip and the expectation has been he will leave, either permanently or on loan.

Most still think there will be another left-back in Carrick's squad when the transfer window closes on 1 September – but it is by no means certain.

articles.summary: El canterano ha firmado un muy buen comienzo de curso
articles.body: El 25 de agosto de 2025, Rafael Garrido se encontraba preparando la temporada con el Atlético Malagueño en Segunda RFEF. Era el titular para Juanfran Funes, pero su aparición por el primer equipo no se hacía presagiar teniendo en cuenta que Sergio Pellicer contaba en plantilla con Carlos Puga y Jokin Gabilondo en su posición. El canterano de Torre del Mar (Vélez-Málaga) no participó con los mayores hasta la jornada 8, cuando entró unos pocos minutos en la derrota del Málaga en El Sardinero por tres a cero. Desde entonces, era octubre, su progresión en el club boquerón ha sido meteórica. La siguiente jornada, la ausencia de Puga, provocó su entrada en el once adelantando a Jokin Gabilondo y siendo titular ante el líder, el Deportivo de la Coruña, en una abultada victoria malaguista por tres a cero. El joven defensa no soltó el puesto hasta la salida de Pellicer. Con Funes y su aterrizaje en el primer equipo, bajó de nuevo al filial aunque el de Loja lo reclutó pronto ante la plaga de lesiones en el lateral zurdo. A pesar de ser diestro y de tener 21 años, Rafita rompió todos los esquemas y nadie lo pudo mover del once titular del equipo hasta el ascenso final a Primera en Almería. Ahora, con el cuadro malaguista ya en la máxima categoría, el Málaga buscó reforzar el lateral zurdo y devolver a Rafita a su puesto natural. Sin embargo, a pesar del fichaje de José Salinas, el joven defensa malaguista ha ganado la partida a su par en estas dos primeras jornadas cuajando dos enormes partidos ante el Atlético de Madrid en el Metropolitano y ante el Dépor en La Rosaleda. En Madrid, en su debut en Primera ante los Baena, Lookman y compañía, Rafita cuajó una actuación notable ganando ocho de sus diez duelos en el partido y cerrando el partido como uno de los jugadores malaguistas con más metros recorridos y un excelente 88% porcentaje de pase. Unos números que no fueron casualidad después de lo visto este lunes en La Rosaleda. El lateral volvió a ser clave para Funes. En defensa ganó el 90% de los duelos y provocó la pena máxima en el área gallega que significó el gol del empate del Málaga obra de Chupete. Su estreno en Primera ha sido sobresaliente y el cuadro de Martiricos tiene bien atado su futuro con el de la Axarquía con un contrato hasta junio de 2029.

articles.body: Ya es oficial, el Manchester United ha confirmado la llegada de Carlos Baleba, futbolista camerunés del Brighton. Firma hasta junio de 2031, con la posibilidad de un año más. Llega a Mánchester a cambio de casi 76 millones de euros. Los 'red devils' siguen reforzando su centro del campo. Tras las llegadas de Tielemans y Andrey Santos, se une a ellos Baleba para completar un tridente de garantías. La temporada pasada fue el sexto jugador de la Premier que más entradas e intercepciones realizó, sumado a su cuarto puesto en conducciones progresivas. Pilar fundamental en la medular del Brighton que se clasificó a Conference. Solo la Copa África le privó de jugar más partidos. Otra gran venta del club, que se convierte en la segunda más cara en su historia, solo superada por Caicedo en 2023. El nuevo fichaje del club cuenta con la bendición de una de las randes leyendas del United, Wayne Rooney. “Me gusta mucho, creo que es un fichaje realmente bueno”, afirmó en Stick to United With Wayne Rooney. "Es un jugador muy bueno que mejorará muchísimo al equipo. Será interesante con Tielemans, Santos y Mainoo, añadió el exfutbolista.
